title: Maximum Principles Harnack and Liouville in Rn

items.title: Subharmonic and superharmonic functions in rn
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $u:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ belong to $C^2(\Omega)$. With the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], $u$ is **subharmonic** when $\Delta u\ge0$ at every point, and **superharmonic** when $\Delta u\le0$. Thus $u$ is harmonic exactly when both conditions hold, and $u$ is superharmonic exactly when $-u$ is subharmonic. Here a **domain** means a nonempty connected open set. This is the classical $C^2$ convention; the equivalence with local mean inequalities is established in the mean-inequality lemma.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Strict subharmonic perturbation
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$, $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and $u\in C^2(\Omega)$ be subharmonic. For $\varepsilon>0$, put $u_\varepsilon(x)=u(x)+\varepsilon|x|^2$. Then $\Delta u_\varepsilon\ge2n\varepsilon>0$, and $u_\varepsilon$ has no interior local maximum.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Weak maximum principle for the laplacian
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be bounded, nonempty and open. If $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ and $\Delta u\ge0$, then
$$\max_{\overline\Omega}u=\max_{\partial\Omega}u.$$
No connectedness or boundary smoothness is required.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: Theorem 2.17 and following subharmonic extension, pp.27–28

items.title: Weak minimum principle for the laplacian
items.statement: For $n\ge2$, a bounded nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ with $\Delta u\le0$ satisfy $\min_{\overline\Omega}u=\min_{\partial\Omega}u$.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Comparison principle for classical subharmonic functions
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be bounded, nonempty and open, and let $u,v\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$. If $\Delta u\ge\Delta v$ in $\Omega$ and $u\le v$ on $\partial\Omega$, then $u\le v$ on $\overline\Omega$.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Classical subharmonic mean value inequalities
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, as in the cited polar-coordinate theorem. Let $n\ge2$ and $u\in C^2(\Omega)$, where $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is open. If $\Delta u\ge0$, then for every $\overline B_r(a)\subset\Omega$, $r>0$,
$$u(a)\le\frac1{|\partial B_r|}\int_{\partial B_r(a)}u\,dS,\qquad u(a)\le\frac1{|B_r|}\int_{B_r(a)}u\,dx.$$
Both inequalities reverse for $\Delta u\le0$. Conversely, either family of local mean inequalities, for all sufficiently small radii at every center, implies the corresponding Laplacian inequality.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (2014)
Tsogtgerel Gantumur, Harmonic functions (2012)

items.title: Strong maximum principle for classical subharmonic functions
items.statement: Assume countable choice for the mean-inequality input. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a domain, and let $u\in C^2(\Omega)$ satisfy $\Delta u\ge0$. If there is $a\in\Omega$ with $u(x)\le u(a)$ for every $x\in\Omega$, then $u$ is constant.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Strong maximum principle for harmonic functions
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a domain, and let $u\in C^2(\Omega)$ be harmonic. If $u$ attains a global maximum or a global minimum at a point of $\Omega$, it is constant.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Nonnegative harmonic function with an interior zero vanishes
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$ and let $u\ge0$ be harmonic on a domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. Then either $u\equiv0$ or $u(x)>0$ for every $x\in\Omega$.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Uniqueness for the classical dirichlet problem
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be bounded, nonempty and open. Two functions $u,v\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ with $\Delta u=\Delta v$ in $\Omega$ and $u=v$ on $\partial\Omega$ agree on $\overline\Omega$. Thus prescribed classical Poisson equation and Dirichlet data have at most one such solution. Moreover, for equal Laplacians,
$$\sup_{\overline\Omega}|u-v|\le\sup_{\partial\Omega}|u-v|.$$
In particular, a sequence of such solutions with a common Laplacian and uniformly convergent boundary traces converges uniformly on the closure.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (2014)
Tsogtgerel Gantumur, Harmonic functions (2012)

items.title: Poisson supremum estimate from a quadratic barrier
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be bounded, nonempty and open, with $\Omega\subset\{x:0<x_1<d\}$ for some $d>0$. If $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ and $L=\sup_\Omega|\Delta u|<\infty$, then
$$\sup_{\overline\Omega}|u|\le\sup_{\partial\Omega}|u|+\frac{d^2}{2}L.$$

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Interior sphere condition and sphere normal
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $p\in\partial\Omega$. An **interior tangent ball at $p$** is a ball $B_R(a)\subset\Omega$ with $R>0$ and $|p-a|=R$. Existence of such a ball is the **interior sphere condition**. Its supplied outward sphere direction is $\nu=(p-a)/R$.

For a real function defined on $B_R(a)\cup\{p\}$, the outward directional derivative, when the following finite limit exists, is
$$\partial_\nu u(p)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{u(p)-u(p-t\nu)}t.$$
The points $p-t\nu$ are in the ball for $0<t<2R$. This definition uses a specified sphere, without assuming a differentiable boundary or a normal field on all of $\partial\Omega$.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Interior sphere barrier for the laplacian
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, $R>0$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\alpha\ge2n/R^2$. Set
$$c=(e^{-\alpha R^2/4}-e^{-\alpha R^2})^{-1},\qquad v(x)=c(e^{-\alpha|x-a|^2}-e^{-\alpha R^2}).$$
On the annulus $R/2<|x-a|<R$, $v$ is subharmonic; it equals $1$ on the inner sphere and $0$ on the outer sphere. At every point of the outer sphere its outward sphere derivative is strictly negative.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Hopf boundary point lemma for the laplacian
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and suppose $B_R(a)\subset\Omega$ is an interior tangent ball at $p\in\partial\Omega$. Let $u\in C^2(\Omega)$ be subharmonic, with a continuous extension to $\overline B_R(a)$, such that $u(x)<M$ for every $x\in\Omega$ and $u(p)=M$. If the finite derivative $\partial_
u u(p)$ exists for $
u=(p-a)/R$, then $\partial_
u u(p)>0$.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Harnack inequality on a ball
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, $R>0$, and let $u\ge0$ be harmonic on $B_R(a)\subset\mathbb R^n$. For every $x\in B_R(a)$,
$$u(x)\le\left(\frac R{R-|x-a|}\right)^n u(a).$$
For $0\le r<R$, set $m=\lceil4r/(R-r)\rceil+1$ and $C=2^{nm}$. Then $C^{-1}u(a)\le u(x)\le Cu(a)$ whenever $|x-a|\le r$. No trace on $\partial B_R(a)$ is assumed.

references.title: Tsogtgerel Gantumur, Harmonic functions (2012)
John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (2014)

items.title: Finite harnack chain on a compact connected subset
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a domain, and let $K\subset\Omega$ be compact, possibly empty or disconnected. There is a finite nonempty family $\{B_{r_j}(a_j)\}_{j=1}^N$ covering $K$, with $r_j>0$ and $\overline B_{4r_j}(a_j)\subset\Omega$, whose overlap graph is connected. An edge means that the two open balls intersect. The family depends only on $K$ and $\Omega$.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (2014)
Tsogtgerel Gantumur, Harmonic functions (2012)

items.title: Harnack inequality on compact subsets
items.statement:
For $n\ge2$, a domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and a nonempty compact $K\subset\Omega$, there is $C=C(K,\Omega,n)\ge1$ such that every nonnegative harmonic function $u$ on $\Omega$ satisfies
$$\sup_Ku\le C\inf_Ku.$$
The compact set $K$ need not be connected.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (2014)
Tsogtgerel Gantumur, Harmonic functions (2012)

items.title: Harnack convergence principle
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a domain, and let $u_1\le u_2\le\cdots$ be real harmonic functions on $\Omega$. Either $u_j(x)\to+\infty$ for every $x\in\Omega$, or the sequence converges uniformly on each compact subset of $\Omega$ to a harmonic function.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Smooth sphere data have a harmonic replacement
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, $R>0$, and $g\in C^\infty(\partial B_R(a))$ be real. Write $\omega_{n-1}=|S^{n-1}|$. There is a unique $h\in C^\infty(B_R(a))\cap C(\overline B_R(a))$ harmonic inside and equal to $g$ on the sphere. It is
$$h(x)=\int_{\partial B_R(a)}\frac{R^2-|x-a|^2}{R\omega_{n-1}|x-y|^n}\,g(y)\,dS(y),\qquad |x-a|<R.$$
The kernel is positive and has integral one at each interior point.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Derivative estimate proof of one sided harmonic liouville
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$, $R>0$, and $u$ be real harmonic on $B_R(a)$. If $S=\sup_{B_R(a)}|u|<\infty$, then $|\nabla u(a)|\le nS/R$. If $u\ge0$, the stronger estimate $|\nabla u(a)|\le nu(a)/R$ holds without assuming a finite global supremum. Consequently, a nonnegative entire harmonic function has gradient zero everywhere.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (2014)
Tsogtgerel Gantumur, Harmonic functions (2012)

items.title: Liouville theorem for bounded harmonic functions
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$ and $u:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be harmonic. If $u$ is bounded above or bounded below on all of $\mathbb R^n$, then $u$ is constant.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Positive entire harmonic functions are constant
items.statement: For $n\ge2$, every nonnegative harmonic function on $\mathbb R^n$ is constant; this includes the zero function as well as strictly positive functions.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Entire harmonic functions with bounded gradient are affine
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$. If $u:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is harmonic and $\sup_x|\nabla u(x)|<\infty$, then $u(x)=b+c\cdot x$ for some $b\in\mathbb R$ and $c\in\mathbb R^n$.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: Theorem 2.7 and Corollary 2.8 p.23, applied to harmonic derivatives

items.title: Removable singularity for bounded harmonic functions
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and $p\in\Omega$. If $u\in C^2(\Omega\setminus\{p\})$ is harmonic and bounded in some punctured neighborhood of $p$, it has a unique harmonic extension to $\Omega$. More generally the same conclusion holds under $u(x)=o(|x-p|^{2-n})$ for $n\ge3$, or $u(x)=o(\log(1/|x-p|))$ for $n=2$, as $x\to p$.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Maximum principle with limsup control at infinity
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be unbounded and open, and let $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ be subharmonic. Suppose $M\in\mathbb R$, $u\le M$ on $\partial\Omega$, and
$$\limsup_{\substack{x\in\Omega\\ |x|\to\infty}}u(x)\le M.$$
Here the last condition means that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $R_0$ with $u(x)\le M+\varepsilon$ whenever $x\in\Omega$ and $|x|>R_0$. Then $u\le M$ on $\overline\Omega$, even if $\partial\Omega$ is empty.

references.title: Thomas Schmidt, Lectures Notes, PDE
references.locator: §2.4 Remarks (on Phragmen-Lindelof principles), (1), printed p.22 / PDF p.24

items.title: Maximum principles need domain and boundary hypotheses
items.statement:
The weak principle requires boundedness and continuity on the full closure; it allows disconnected open sets. Its conclusion is an attained boundary maximum for subharmonic functions. The strong harmonic principle instead uses connectedness and an attained **global** interior extremum; neither boundedness nor a boundary trace is needed. These are the distinct scopes of [[thm-weak-maximum-principle-for-the-laplacian]] and [[thm-strong-maximum-principle-for-harmonic-functions]].

At a boundary point, [[thm-hopf-boundary-point-lemma-for-the-laplacian]] needs an interior tangent ball, a strict interior inequality, continuity on its closure, and existence of the supplied outward directional derivative. It gives a positive outward derivative at a maximum; negating the function reverses the sign at a minimum.

Unbounded sets can be treated by [[thm-maximum-principle-with-limsup-control-at-infinity]] if the same finite upper bound controls the boundary and the limsup at infinity. No open-mapping or general boundary-normal theorem is asserted here.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

title: Maximum Principles Harnack and Liouville in Rn — Examples

items.title: Harmonic function attaining only boundary extrema
items.statement: For $n\ge2$, $u(x)=x_1$ on $\overline B_1(0)\subset\mathbb R^n$ is harmonic. Its maximum $1$ and minimum $-1$ occur only at $e_1$ and $-e_1$, respectively, on the boundary. At $e_1$ its outward sphere derivative is $1$.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: Theorems 2.17 and Lemma 2.21, pp.27–30, affine specialization

items.title: Harnack constant from the poisson kernel ratio
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, $R>0$, and $u\ge0$ be harmonic on $B_R(0)$. For $x\in B_R(0)$ and $t=|x|/R$,
$$\frac{1-t}{(1+t)^{n-1}}u(0)\le u(x)\le\frac{1+t}{(1-t)^{n-1}}u(0).$$
These kernel bounds require no boundary trace at radius $R$.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Maximum principle fails for superharmonic maxima
items.statement: The assertion that every superharmonic $u\in C^2(B_1)\cap C(\overline B_1)$ has its maximum on $\partial B_1$ is false, for every $n\ge2$. A witness is $u(x)=-|x|^2$.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Weak maximum principle needs boundedness or control at infinity
items.statement: Without boundedness or control at infinity, a harmonic function continuous on the closure of an open set and zero on its nonempty boundary need not be nonpositive inside. For $n\ge2$, take $\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ and $u(x)=x_n$.

references.title: Thomas Schmidt, Lectures Notes, PDE
references.locator: §2.4 Remarks (on Phragmen-Lindelof principles), (1), printed p.22 / PDF p.24

items.title: Hopf lemma needs a boundary geometry hypothesis
items.statement:
An accessible outward directional derivative at a strict boundary maximum need not be positive when there is no interior tangent ball. In the plane, for $x>0$ put $r=(x^2+y^2)^{1/2}$, $\theta=\arctan(y/x)$, and
$$u(x,y)=\frac{x\log r+y\theta}{(\log r)^2+\theta^2},\qquad \Omega=\{(x,y):x>0,\ 0<r<1/2,\ u(x,y)<0\}.$$
Then $\Omega$ is a domain, $u$ is harmonic there and extends continuously to its closure with $u(0,0)=0$. It is strictly negative inside, its outward derivative along $-e_1$ at zero is zero, and no interior tangent ball exists there.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Liouville needs one sided boundedness
items.statement: For $n\ge2$, an entire real harmonic function need not be constant without a one-sided bound. The coordinate function $u(x)=x_1$ is a counterexample.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions
references.locator: §5 Corollary 6 and Exercise 10, p.8, affine hypothesis test

items.title: Unbounded punctured harmonic singularity is not removable
items.statement: A harmonic function on a punctured ball need not have a harmonic extension at the puncture without growth control. On $0<|x|<1$, use $u(x)=\log|x|$ for $n=2$ and $u(x)=|x|^{2-n}$ for $n\ge3$. Neither has even a continuous extension at zero.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Strong maximum principle needs connectedness
items.statement: For $n\ge2$, the connectedness hypothesis cannot be omitted from the strong harmonic maximum principle. Let $\Omega=B_1(0)\cup B_1(3e_1)$, and set $u=1$ on the first ball and $u=0$ on the second. It attains an interior global maximum without being globally constant.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations

items.title: Hopf conclusion needs a strict nonconstant extremum
items.statement: For $n\ge2$, a boundary maximum and an interior sphere alone do not force a strictly positive outward derivative. On $\overline B_1(0)$, the harmonic function $u\equiv0$ attains its maximum at every boundary point and has outward derivative zero there.

references.title: Gantumur, Harmonic functions

items.title: Subharmonic quartic and harmonic saddle
items.statement: For $n\ge2$, on $\overline B_1(0)$ the function $q(x)=|x|^4$ is subharmonic and lies below the harmonic function $h\equiv1$ having the same boundary values. The function $s(x)=x_1^2-x_2^2$ is harmonic and has a saddle at the origin, despite $\nabla s(0)=0$.

references.title: Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations
